description: We’re Computer Science students from the University of Malaya, passionate about using technology to solve real-world problems. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we chose “Be an Earth System Trend Detective!” to explore NASA Earth data, identify environmental trends, and turn complex data into clear insights using data analysis, machine learning, and visualization.
summary:
What would have been the outcome of our decision in 1985, when it was possible to choose another path for our planet? What would happen if we had more plants planted, fewer industrial emissions, no forest fires, and no deforestation?
This is what the idea behind the project Habitat Rewind is all about. Habitat Rewind is an interactive scientific game that helps explore these questions. In the habitat rewind game, which uses the Earth Observation Data for 1985 to 2025 provided by NASA, you travel back in time, discover the changes in the ecosystem, take environmental actions to learn about the outcome of our actions if we were to change them.
The signals that our planet sends us through the increase of temperatures, the changes in the ecosystems and the rise in environmental pressure that we are experiencing now are obvious enough. Project habitat rewind aims to transform these scientific facts into an interesting story helping people understand its importance and take action on time.
It is impossible to rewind our history on earth but rewinding our history can give us some valuable lessons about our mistakes that our ancestors made. It is still possible to save our earth but if we keep postponing our actions, we will never get the chance to repair the damages done by our wrongs. “Habitat Rewind” seeks to tell everybody about it.
details:
Habitat Rewind's Project Solution:

Habitat Rewind is an educational data exploration game that seeks to educate people on how their actions regarding the environment can affect the outcome of the climate through real NASA satellite data turned into a counterfactual game. The players go around different ecosystems around the world, become data detectives and discover real-world climate patterns and utilize strategy mechanics to "rewind" back to 1985 to address climate problems.

How does our Solution work?

Within the game, the player plays the role of a climate detective who faces biomes that change and fluctuating weather conditions around the world. The game involves the player embarking on a quest to discover what is really happening environmentally in the different regions, which include warming, changing rainfall, and deforestation. Through the process, the player uses actual data from NASA and rewinds the situation to solve it.

Warming and Wetting (Malaysia Highlands)

The gamer takes the trip to the central highlands of Malaysia that have undergone changes from a seasonal savanna to a tropical rainforest as a result of the warming and the increase in rainfall. The gamer checks whether the "rainier" trend is valid or not by comparing the climate data of NASA MERRA-2 against GPCP v2.3 satellite data. Within the game, gamers are asked to make the temperature average by going back to 1985 and handling the budget:

Level 1: Grow more trees to increase forest coverage.

Level 2: Reduce industrial emissions to lower the temperature while preventing too much rainfall.

Players get to know about the influence of reforestation and reduction of emissions on the temperature in this way.

Deforestation and Soil Health (New Mexico):

Also the player gets introduced to New Mexico Mountains with particular attention to deforestation and changes in biomes. The player will be able to find out if deforestation in the past two decades is real by using satellite imagery of NASA's MODIS. To add more interaction to this, the player has to create a counterfactual simulation in which:

Task: Imposing "Stop Deforestation" laws from 1985 to 2025.

Players will get to see time-lapse animation showing their scenario along with historical data to see how much effect would preservation of the forest have on the region for the next four decades.

Extreme Heat and Aridity (Mogollon Rim, Arizona):
Now comes the Mogollon Rim, which poses challenging conditions due to too much heat and drying out of the area. This gives the player an opportunity to understand the work done by the scientists to monitor the land surface temperatures based on the climate drivers from NASA's POWER.

Task: Reduce the amount of methane emissions on a global scale (methane is reducing faster in the atmosphere than CO2).

After the player completes all the tasks, the player gets access to Sandbox Mode and Data Explorer.

The game benefits

Students, Climate enthusiasts and general population by

a)demonstrating the impact of the world's climate activities and actions, such as reforestations and emission cuts.

b)combining NASA's data and the history of its effects in a fun way.

c) teaching the players how to determine what climate information is true through actual climate data.

Our Goal:

Even though it is possible for our participants to go back in time and change the course of history, it is not within our capabilities to do so in real life. All we hope to accomplish by going back in time using a time machine through our game is to learn from history about the effect of human activities on the environment. We aim to teach people how the world would have changed over the past 40 years if actions such as reforestation, no deforestation, and reduction in emissions had been taken. We want to ensure that the information collected by NASA is accessible to everyone.

Tools and Technologies used:

App (Front-End):

  • React 18, TypeScript & Vite → for the front-end framework, enabling strict development mode and fast build times with React Router as navigation.
  • Zustand & Recharts → as the state manager and dynamic chart renderer.
  • three.js, d3-geo & Leaflet → as the 3D globe, scene and 2D map renderer using OpenStreetMap tiles.

Data Pipeline (Back-End & Processing):

  • Python (3.11+) →used to process data, with pandas, numpy, and scipy used for handling the data, regression analysis and confidence intervals.
  • pymannkendall → used to perform modified Mann-Kendall trend test and Sen slope calculations for climate data.
  • xarray, netCDF4, rasterio & pyreadr →for handling different scientific data formats such as GISTEMP netCDF files, forest tiles and biome polygons.
  • Jupyter ecosystem → for recomputing data results programmatically through nbformat, nbclient, and matplotlib

Testing, Workflow & Hosting:

  • Vitest & pytest → for front end and back end tests and a custom validate_outputs.py file to check data correctness.
  • GitHub & Vercel → for versioning (using branch-per-track workflow) and deploying the web app.
  • Claude Code → for AI-assisted development workflows.

Data Source:

The primary source of data for our project will be NASA POWER, which provides us with monthly data on temperature and rainfall ranging from 1985 to 2025 as historical data for our game. The reliability of the above-mentioned information is determined through NASA GISTEMP v4 and NOAA GPCP v2.3. In terms of observing the extent of tree cover, reforestation and the temperature of the land surface, we will make use of NASA MODIS (MOD44B & MOD11A2), supplied by ORNL DAAC, and further fire and deforestation information will be provided through NASA FIRMS and Hansen Global Forest Change. Finally, our cumulative emissions scenario model will be provided by the data from the Global Carbon Budget and Our World in Data.

Character Design:

three.js, d3-geo & Leaflet → for building the 3D globe, base scenes, and 2D map views using OpenStreetMap tiles.
